Implements the cascade specified in ADR-010 (`docs/decisions/010-cascade.md`). ## Background ADR-010 decided how to combine the three pillars we already have — the owned DOM (ADR-007), selector matching (ADR-008), and stylesheet parsing (ADR-009) — into a per-element `ComputedStyle`. This is the last structural piece before layout and paint: after this, `h1 { color: red }` is a fact about a concrete `dom::Element`, not just text. ## Scope ### New files - `src/renderer/css/cascade.hpp` — public types and the `cascade()` function - `src/renderer/css/cascade.cpp` — implementation - `tests/test_cascade.cpp` — unit tests ### Types - `CascadeValue { std::string value; bool important; Specificity specificity; size_t source_order; }` - `ComputedStyle { unordered_map declarations; bool has(string); optional get(string); }` - `ComputedStyleMap = unordered_map` ### Public API `ComputedStyleMap cascade(const Stylesheet&, const dom::Document&)` ### Algorithm 1. Pre-order DFS over the DOM (document order, parents before children). 2. For each element: - Walk all rules in source order. - For each rule, for each selector in its `SelectorList`, check `matches(element)`. - For each matching selector's rule, for each `Declaration`, compute the `(important, specificity, source_order)` coordinate and keep the winner per property. - Then run the inheritance pass: for each of the seven inherited properties not explicitly set on this element, copy from the parent's `ComputedStyle` (if the parent has one). - Store the resulting `ComputedStyle` in the map. ### Inherited properties (v1) - `color` - `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-style`, `font-weight` - `line-height` - `visibility` All other properties take no value when no rule applies (unset in `ComputedStyle`). ### Behavior (from ADR-010's table) - `p { color: red }` on `

` → empty `ComputedStyle` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `renderer/css/cascade.{hpp,cpp}` compile into `honeybee_lib` - [ ] Tests in `tests/test_cascade.cpp` cover every row of ADR-010's behavior table - [ ] `!important` beats normal declarations at any specificity - [ ] Specificity beats source order at the same importance - [ ] Source order breaks ties at the same importance and specificity - [ ] The seven inherited properties propagate to descendants - [ ] An element's own declaration beats an inherited one - [ ] `grep -rl "lexbor/" src/` still returns exactly `src/renderer/html/convert.cpp` - [ ] `renderer::dom` and `renderer::css::SelectorList` untouched - [ ] CI green ## Two-commit plan - **Commit 1 — matching + specificity ordering**: `cascade()` walks the DOM and stylesheet, resolves per-property winners using `(important, specificity, source_order)`, stores `ComputedStyle` in the map. No inheritance yet. - **Commit 2 — inheritance + typed getters**: second pass for the seven inherited properties; `ComputedStyle::get()` with fallback semantics documented. Each commit independently reviewable; CI isolates any failure to a specific half. ## Refs - ADR-010: `docs/decisions/010-cascade.md` - ADR-009: `docs/decisions/009-css-parser.md` - ADR-008: `docs/decisions/008-css-selectors.md` - ADR-007: `docs/decisions/007-dom-ownership.md`
